ABB launches IRB 1700 and 1700ID for precision manufacturing

Five variants carry 6–12 kilograms; performance improvements remain manufacturer claims.

ABB / RoboticsTomorrow ↗12 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

New manufacturing models

ABB announced the IRB 1700 and IRB 1700ID for their public debut at CIIF in Shanghai on October 12–16. Five variants carry 6–12 kilograms and use OmniCore controllers, targeting handling, welding, finishing and machine tending.

Accuracy and installation

ABB specifies path repeatability down to 0.03 millimetres and joint speeds up to 700 degrees per second. The footprint is 50% smaller than the predecessor, while the 1700ID routes cables and hoses internally.

Validate on the intended task

Claims include up to 20% shorter cycles, 15% lower power consumption and oil-change intervals up to 20,000 hours. These manufacturer figures do not guarantee every cell’s results; tooling, paths and production timing still matter.
